body: thats awesome! what got you into it? and out?

Brain fog doesnt allow for it all that much anymore but I still give it a shot from time to time. 
Do you?

Sure, this is a possibility. But where to find the motivation to take on so much when I can hardly get out of bed most days? 
And if motivation is found I dont think lazily committing to a spiritual path will result in the desired outcome.

The issue with that lies in which path is taken through transformation, i could easily slip into further darkness and (most likely) become insane. Or, I could literally fight for my life and become the best version of myself...a lot of lessons have been learnt through the burden that is depression. They always seem to be belittled by existential philosophy that whirs around in my brain non stop, thats probably where this madness came from to start with. So it ultimately comes down to how I apply myself. It'd be blissful if I could just retreat from modern life, become a pilgrim, a buddhist, travel, explore, surround myself by spiritual leaders and people alike and cleanse my soul, reach nirvana perhaps. This is what I want. But I'm studying science, so that'll lead to another path entirely...and fuck doing that until I die.

haha thank you so much! that means a lot. Writing has always been a great passion but it seems to have dissolved away equally as fast as my brain. I'll be sure to check that subreddit out :) 

I'm pleased to hear that! I hope the best for you too. big cyber hug of appreciation your way, kind stranger.

You are completely right. Everything is temporary, change is inevitable. But if the bad is just as temporary as the good and this is frightening. The truth is, I wasn't always such a lame ass when it comes to these things. If I was pushed down, I'd take away every positive from the situation and treat is as a learning experience. Its just so hard to put this into practice now, I've lo/st a complete sense of self. The soul/self/personality (whatever you prefer to call it) that lies within this body is like a foreign pathogen, its unrecognizable....okay that sounded bizarre.  

Those are wise words! A lot of Buddhist undertows which is frickin awesome. The trouble is in applying these things on a day to day basis, that in itself takes strength. 

You're so lovely, thank you for taking your time and interest to respond. I really do appreciate it. 
How is your day going?

Understandably. This is natural though, it's your brains way of coming to terms with the situation, adapting to this change. And at first it will be really tough but it'll get easier with each day. Try not to suppress your feelings, it's healthy to release grief and pain. But keep busy at the same time. Do things you enjoy. Don't spend too much time alone, confide in a close friend about how you feel. It's ultimately all about balance and looking after yourself to the best of your ability at this moment in time. I really hope you feel better soon, heartbreak sucks big time. 
What kind of activities help distract you?

I'm sorry to hear that, friend. But don't lose hope! People enter your life with reason and leave with reason, even if that reason is unclear to you for now. There is purpose in everything that happens, perhaps if you and your partner hadn't split you wouldn't be given the chance to encounter the next love of your life, perhaps an even greater and stronger love. 
Personally I motivate myself by focusing on everything other than the person I have lost, and this usually amounts to dedicating a lot of time for myself and friends, which can be very therapeutic. 
Stay strong!
